oats.definition: A cereal grain commonly used in porridge and baked foods.

quinoa.definition: Small edible seeds cooked and used in meals like a grain.

buckwheat.definition: Edible seeds used like a grain or ground into flour.

toast.definition: Bread heated until its surface becomes brown and crisp.

spaghetti.definition: Pasta made in long thin strands.

ramen.definition: Japanese-style wheat noodles, often served in broth.

yogurt.definition: A thick dairy food made by fermenting milk with bacteria.

tofu.definition: A soft or firm food made by coagulating soy milk into curds.

chicken.definition: Meat from a chicken, sold as a whole bird or in cuts.

turkey.definition: Meat from a turkey, sold as a whole bird or in cuts.

wing.definition: A poultry wing sold or served as a cut of meat.

thigh.definition: The upper part of a poultry leg, sold as a cut of meat.

roast.definition: A large cut of meat intended for cooking with dry heat.

tuna.definition: Meat from a large sea fish, commonly sold fresh or canned.

crab.definition: A shellfish with a hard shell and claws, sold as food.

mussel.definition: An edible shellfish with two dark elongated shells.

salami.definition: A cured sausage, often sliced and eaten cold.

fillet.definition: A boneless portion of meat or fish.

shank.definition: A cut of meat from the lower part of an animal's leg.

bamboo.definition: A textile made from fibers derived from bamboo plants.

jute.definition: A strong plant fiber used to make coarse cloth, sacks, and rope.

alpaca.definition: A soft textile fiber obtained from alpacas, or fabric made from it.

polyester.definition: A synthetic fiber used to make fabrics and other products.

rayon.definition: A manufactured fiber made from processed cellulose.

microfiber.definition: Fabric made from very fine synthetic fibers.

brocade.definition: A rich fabric with raised patterns woven into it.

weave.definition: The pattern in which threads are interlaced to form fabric.

weight.definition: How heavy a fabric is for a given area.

stretch.definition: The ability of a fabric to extend when pulled.

breathability.definition: The ability of a fabric to allow air or moisture vapor to pass through.

hand-wash.definition: To wash clothing by hand rather than in a machine.

iron.definition: To smooth wrinkles in fabric with a heated iron.

steam.definition: To use steam to refresh fabric or remove wrinkles.

bleach.definition: To whiten fabric or remove color using a bleaching agent.

line-dry.definition: To dry clothing by hanging it on a line.

fabric-softener.definition: A laundry product used to make washed fabric feel softer.

marble.definition: A hard stone with patterns or veins, used in buildings and sculpture.

silver.definition: A precious silvery-white metal used in jewelry and other products.

linen.definition: Fabric made from fibers of the flax plant.

denim.definition: A strong cotton fabric commonly used to make jeans.

polyester.definition: A synthetic fiber used to make fabrics and other products.

velvet.definition: A fabric with a dense, soft raised surface.

fiberglass.definition: Fine glass fibers used in insulation or to reinforce other materials.

silicone.definition: A heat-resistant synthetic material used in sealants, molds, and many other products.

resin.definition: A natural or synthetic substance that can be used in coatings, adhesives, or molded products.

insulation.definition: Material used to reduce the transfer of heat, sound, or electricity.
